messages:
incident-bot: Pager triggered -> SEV 1: GPU_SIGBUS_BURST on gpu-pool-west2a (policy: autopager-v2). count=18 in 2m, affected pools: model-infer-prod, embed-svc.
pagerduty: Incident created and routed to eng-oncall -> PD#PD-87912, escalation policy: gpu-ops.
maya: ack'ing the page, jumping in.  starting triage. which region?
own: west2a. seeing a flurry of SIGBUS in the runtime logs, likely cudnn/cublas or node-level memory corruption. logs here: `gs://redwood-logs/gpu/west2a/3123459999.log`
julia: I see nodes reporting `CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS` + `SIGBUS` in dmesg on 3/6 gpus on node gpu-wn-137. Also kernel driver reset on one.
raman: any recent driver upgrades or kernel modules changed?
own: nope, no rolling driver changes in last 24h. autoscaler bumped up a few pools ~10m ago.
maya: quick impact check: metrics show p95 latency spike on generation endpoints and ~7% 5xx rate on embeddings for a 30s window, then cascading failures as jobs retried. customer-facing: a small number of customers hitting degraded embedding responses.
maya: mitigation idea 1: temporarily reroute traffic off west2a to west2b CPU fallback pool for critical tenants. 2: cordon affected nodes and drain GPUs to kill bad processes. 3: reduce batch sizes / disable prefetch to reduce mem pressure.
julia: starting cordon/drain now for nodes tagged `gpu:wn-137*`. command: `kubectl cordon gpu-wn-137 && kubectl drain gpu-wn-137 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=2m`
raman: also add auto-fallback at the router for embeddings: `route set embed-svc --region west2a --fallback west2b --min-healthy 3`
own: applying fallback rule, will patch in 30s.
incident-bot: PD-87912 acknowledged by maya. escalation timer paused.
maya: I'm going to scale down the kvcache prefetcher on embed-svc in west2a: `PATCH /config/embed-svc {"kvcache_prefetch":false, "batch_size": 32}` — doing a canary first (1 pod).
owen: logs snippet from gpu-wn-137 (tail):
```
[2026-03-15T14:07:12Z] runtime: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS in /opt/runtime/lib/libcudnn.so:0x7f4c3a2b
[2026-03-15T14:07:12Z] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, PID 48321, Invalid memory access during SM emulation
[2026-03-15T14:07:13Z] process[48321]: sigbus (code=1, addr=0x7ffc1e9a8000)
```
maya: that Xid 31 points to a GPU page fault/illegal memory access. Could be bad user model, driver, or hardware.
julia: we should repro on a quarantined node: taking gpu-wn-138 offline and running a stress infer job from the failing tenant. if it reproduces, we have deterministic failure.
raman: good. I'll request a hardware check on gpu-wn-137/138 (NVIDIA diagnostics). filing ticket to infra: `infra-ticket create --nodes gpu-wn-137,gpu-wn-138 --symptom "SIGBUS Xid31"`
escalations-bot: Paging SRE-hw for optional escalation (if hw diag fails) in 15m.
own: fallback patch live, routing volume to west2b CPU fallback up from 0% -> 18% now. Errors on embeddings drop to 1.2% from 7%. latency back to baseline for most tenants.
maya: good. Continue draining the affected nodes and kill any runaway processes. Also keep an eye on memory fragmentation metrics for kvcache.
julia: drained gpu-wn-137 and gpu-wn-138, eviction logs show KV cache invalidations but pods rescheduled to west2b.
raman: NVDIA diag results incoming: nvdiag shows one GPU on gpu-wn-137 with ECC errors and memory reports failing long-run test. probable hardware issue.
own: marking affected GPUs as unhealthy and removing them from pool: `poolctl mark-unhealthy gpu-wn-137:GPU0,gpu-wn-138:GPU1 --reason "ECC+SIGBUS"`
maya: Customer impact: small subset of embedding requests for 4 enterprise tenants experienced increased latency and transient 5xxs for ~3 minutes during the spike, mitigated by reroute. We'll set severity = P1 for oncall response but P2 for long-term impact.
raman: temporary mitigation steps recorded in incident doc. Recommend: 1) replace faulty GPU(s), 2) add more aggressive autodrain thresholds for SIGBUS/Xid 31, 3) add router rule to fallback earlier when error rate >2% for 1m.
own: I'm going to schedule a canary to validate patched prefetch disabled across a subset of nodes in west2b too.
maya: handoff: my shift ends in 40m. owen will take next oncall. owen, please monitor PD-87912, follow up on hardware replacement ETA, and confirm post-fallback stability for 30m.
own: ack. I'll take it. I'll also braindump the checklist to the incident doc.
incident-bot: PD-87912: status updated -> acknowledged (maya). Next escalation timer set for 15m to SRE-hw if no update.
pagerduty: Reminder -> send status update to #incidents-customer-comms if we need to notify customers.
maya: Notifying CS to prepare a brief for affected tenants. pinging @cs-lead.
julia: quick note: I'll open a postmortem ticket with labels [gpu,sigbus,hw-failure,autopager] and assign to runtime + infra.
escalations-bot: Hardware team acknowledged ticket, ETA replace GPU: 18-24 hours (spare part). Will attempt RMA priority.
own: adding follow-up runbook actions: `- add Xid31 detector to autopager` `- lower prefetch defaults` `- add fallback percent threshold`
maya: thanks all. leaving notes in the incident doc. If anything changes escalate to SRE-hw and PD.
julia: last check: 5xxs at baseline, embed error rate 0.9%, gone from spike. closing active mitigation phase.
maya: handing off fully to owen.
own: confirmed, I'll keep watch for 30m and then transition to follow-up.
incident-bot: Thread closed for active mitigations. Postmortem required: yes.
maya: post-incident: schedule blameless postmortem, tag impacted customers and include timeline + mitigation steps.
owen: thanks — will follow up in the incident channel with a short summary and link to the postmortem ticket.
